title: Factored comparison indexed by its diagrams
statement: For two three-arrow diagrams s and t in a category, a comparison means precisely four vertex isomorphisms making all three arrow squares commute. For actual arrows eta from s.obj0 to s.obj3 and theta from t.obj0 to t.obj3, a factored comparison consists of this comparison and equations eta=s.composite and theta=t.composite. It converts to the original FiniteDiscreteFactoredComparison with exactly the same vertices, arrows and equalities, and gives an isomorphism between the total arrows.

proof.text: Define Comparison by the existing FiniteDiscreteThreeStepComparison on the diagram fields. Store the total equations with the composite function rather than its expanded term. Recover the original record by keeping its three fields; its existing nonemptyArrowIso theorem gives the total arrow isomorphism. This is a record representation change, without any existentially chosen data or omitted square.
